lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and holders of 5% or more cannot sell shares for 180 days after the shares first trade on the NYSE American. The underwriters can give written consent to sell, and some exceptions apply.

what: Ga Sai Tong runs three Japanese and French-Japanese restaurants in Tsim Sha Tsui and Causeway Bay, Hong Kong.
proceeds: It expects about $27.6 million in net proceeds. About 40% is for new restaurants in Hong Kong and East Asia, 15% for hiring and training chefs, 15% for upgrading existing restaurants, and 30% for general costs and working capital.
risks: The company's results depend heavily on how well its existing and new restaurants do.
It may fail to manage and promote its restaurants, and damage to its brands could hurt the business.
If it cannot raise enough money for new restaurants, its growth could be badly held back.
Its bank loans can be called back on demand, which could strain its cash and finances.
It may struggle to find good locations, may face higher rents, or may fail to renew leases.
